Shizuku exposes privileged system APIs to user apps without root, by running a small service started via wireless ADB or root. Three compatible providers are supported — Shizuku (RikkaApps), AXManager (Axeron), and Sui (a Magisk/KernelSU module for rooted devices); install any one. Once authorized, ALTIV DEV AI can use the android-shizuku-cli CLI for package, permission, settings, input, and activity management.

Android blocks the accessibility toggle for apps installed from a downloaded APK file. This is an OS security policy, not a ALTIV DEV AI bug — nothing is wrong with your install. Allowing restricted settings only re-enables the toggle; it grants nothing on its own, and you still choose whether to turn the service on.

Runs inside ALTIV DEV AI, without a VPN profile: only ALTIV DEV AI\'s own connections can reach your tailnet, and only while ALTIV DEV AI is running. “Use Subnet Routes” lets addresses that other devices share (such as a home network) go through Tailscale.
Finish signing in in the browser. ALTIV DEV AI comes back by itself.
Turns Tailscale and every proxy route off at once, without a restart: all of ALTIV DEV AI connects as if nothing here were set. Your settings are kept.
ALTIV DEV AI listens on 127.0.0.1 for its own connections. Other apps on this device can reach that port but cannot use it without a password that changes every time ALTIV DEV AI starts.
Turn Tailscale off above to connect directly again, or keep it on and ALTIV DEV AI keeps trying.
